title: README and project documentation
learningObjectives: Explain readme and project documentation and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: A README introduces the project, its purpose, setup steps, scripts, architecture pointers, configuration requirements, and contribution workflow. Documentation should be accurate, maintained with code, and must not reveal credentials or private data.
understand.whyItMatters: Good documentation shortens onboarding and makes future maintenance safer. A stale README can be worse than a concise accurate one.
understand.analogy: A README is the front door and orientation sign for a repository.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The outline covers the information a contributor needs to start and work safely. Actual commands should match the repository configuration.

examples.code:
# Project README outline
## Purpose
## Requirements
## Setup
## Development scripts
## Project structure
## Testing
## Deployment
## Security notes
examples.explanation: The outline covers the information a contributor needs to start and work safely. Actual commands should match the repository configuration.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Write a README for a small web project. Verify every command and link against the current repository before publishing.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.

questions.explanation: Reliable workflows use evidence and plan for failure rather than relying on assumptions.
